Notes: Includes summary cards, cluster status, critical alerts, and the AI Health Summary widget.
Full CRUD operations and detailed views for clusters and hosts are implemented.
Users can view service status and trigger start/stop/restart operations.
Users can view, manage, and define alerts. Detail pages include AI troubleshooting.
A UI exists for viewing and editing service configurations.
A page to view the status and progress of background tasks is implemented.
A dedicated page for searching and filtering logs is available.
Users can manage their profile and application preferences.
All CRUD interfaces for documentation, legal, pricing, testimonials, and FAQs are complete.
Admins can create, edit, and delete users and manage their roles.
A powerful, customizable data table is used across all applications.
The main navigation sidebar is fully functional, with tooltips for the collapsed state.
The floating action button provides quick navigation and actions.
A global search is implemented in the header for finding resources quickly.
A `react-joyride` tour guides new users through the main dashboard.
A consistent light/dark theme is available across all applications.
The framework for i18n is set up with `react-i18next` and language files.
The Genkit flow and UI widget for summarizing cluster health are implemented.
The Genkit flow and UI component for suggesting alert resolutions are implemented.
A `pnpm seed` script is available to populate the database with mock data.
`run.sh`, `kill-ports.sh`, and `clean-workspace.sh` are fully functional.
A suite of Playwright tests covers the main user flows and authentication.
The CI pipeline automatically runs linting, building, and testing on every push.
The Storybook setup is now fixed, but more stories need to be written for full component coverage.
The application currently relies on manual refreshes or query refetching. WebSockets would provide real-time updates for tasks and alerts.
The backend does not yet have APIs for managing HDP/HDF stack versions and repositories.
While E2E tests exist, more granular unit and integration test coverage is needed, especially for backend services.
While a `docker-compose.yml` exists, more robust deployment scripts and configurations (e.g., for Kubernetes or AWS ECS) should be created.
